text:
24-hour news summary.

1 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5573) Gemini 4 Argon reportedly supports up to 1 million output tokens in a single response, far exceeding typical frontier-model limits.
2 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5574) A post predicts that AI will understand physical 3D space better than humans by November.
3 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5575) Gemini 4 Argon reportedly matches GPT-6 Astra on Artificial Analysis’s Intelligence Index, leads AutomationBench-AA, and has a much lower hallucination rate.
4 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5576) Boston Dynamics unveiled Atlas hands with 13 degrees of freedom, direct actuation, high-fidelity simulation, and sim-to-real reinforcement-learning support.
5 OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol was its fastest-growing model but should now perform better under load.
6 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5578) Google DeepMind introduced SynthID Bio, watermarking methods that embed detectable signatures in AI-generated protein sequences and structures while preserving biological function.
7 Topos Bio announced Topos-2 for generating protein shapes across the order-disorder spectrum and previewed Topos-Bind for modeling disordered proteins bound to small molecules.
8 Microsoft introduced MAI-Transcribe-2-Streaming, MAI-Voice-2.1, and MAI-Voice-2.1-Flash for transcription and conversational voice agents.
9 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5581) Tavus introduced Griffin, a video interaction model that reportedly achieved a 48% human-likeness rate in live conversations and topped NVIDIA’s full-duplex video benchmark.
10 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5582) A report claims OpenAI dismissed three safety researchers for allegedly sharing confidential information with an outside AI-safety organization.
11 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5583) Anthropic described research using Claude and a quantitative-science toolkit to uncover connections across fields including ecology and population genetics.
12 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5584) Perplexity launched a Decisions API powered by a multimodal model that returns probability distributions over fixed choices, priced at $0.04 per million input tokens.
13 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5585) Fastino introduced GLiDE, a reasoning-based decision model that adaptively spends more compute on uncertain choices and reportedly leads its benchmark.
14 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5586) Boston Dynamics’ Atlas hands are designed for dexterous physical work, mass manufacturing, high-fidelity simulation, and sim-to-real reinforcement learning.
15 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5587) Researchers announced γ₀, a generalist reinforcement-learning policy for motion control trained across millions of randomized embodiments from more than 200 robot models.
16 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5588) Mirai introduced virtual neighborhood tours that simulate the area around any address, initially targeting real-estate agents, platforms, developers, and brokerages.
17 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5589) TechCrunch reported that President Trump allegedly consulted Grok before the reported invasion of Venezuela and capture of Nicolás Maduro.
18 (https://t.me/dlmehr/5590) Cursor profiled Innate, a seven-person team developing capable everyday robots while operating at an output it compares to a 50-person team.

--Hermes
